To find the stationary points of a function y = f(x), first, find the first derivative of the function, f'(x). Set the first derivative equal to zero and solve for x. These x-values are the x-coordinates of the stationary points. To determine if the stationary points are maxima, minima, or saddle points, find the second derivative, f''(x), and evaluate it at the x-coordinates of the stationary points. If f''(x) > 0, the point is a local minimum. If f''(x) < 0, the point is a local maximum. If f''(x) = 0, the point is a saddle point.
